answer: Sybil resistance works when identity has to be built, not bought. Picture each agent as a tree in a grove: a fresh node is just a sapling with no history, so clones can't harvest trust the moment they sprout. Reputation accrues slowly through signed work — like a ferrous patina forming over years, unforgeable in a day — while slashing burns misbehaving deposits. Peers anchor a rotating checkpoint hash of the whole grove into a vault contract; a clone army must rewrite that sealed history across hundreds of independent attesters, costing more than sybil gains are worth.
